for form inputs\r\nLOCATION:Goudriaan Room I&II · Postillion Hotel & Convention Centre WTC \r\n Rotterdam\\, Rotterdam\r\nDESCRIPTION:We can never get enough of SDC\\, the front-dev friendly API \r\n to implement and share UI components for Drupal. So\\, let’s rejoice tog\r\n ether by discovering the biggest improvement since the introduction of \r\n the API: we will soon be able to implement form elements directly with \r\n SDC\\, only with UI logic and front technologies\\, without messing with \r\n backend APIs.\\n\\nPierre\\, one of the maintainers of SDC in Core\\, will \r\n show you all the cool stuff which can be done with this addition.\\n\\n**\r\n Prerequisite**\\n\\nKnowledge about SDC and components-based theming.  \\n\r\n \\nAnd/or about Drupal Admin UI\\, especially display building tasks (Blo\r\n ck Layout\\, Layout Builder\\, Views...)\\n\\n**Target Audience**\\n\\nFront \r\n developers\\, design system owners\\, ambitious site builders\\n\\n**Outlin\r\n e**\\n\\nThe introduction of SDC to Core in 2023 had a significant impact\r\n  on the Drupal ecosystem by starting a movement to embrace design syste\r\n m methodology\\, helping the front-designers to implement ambitious shar\r\n eable designs\\, and bringing display building back to the forefront.\\n\\\r\n nHowever\\, the UI components related to form inputs can’t be implemente\r\n d as SDC yet and are still managed the old way\\, with abstruse PHP clas\r\n ses.\\n\\nDate picker\\, interactive data table\\, file uploader\\, slider\\,\r\n  toggle\\, draggable tree view… they often constitute around 20% of desi\r\n gn system scopes and their absence is felt heavily by project teams and\r\n  the contrib space.\\n\\nGood news! We will land support to form elements\r\n  in SDC in 2026 and it will be a game changer. Full component libraries\r\n  will be packageable as Drupal themes and shared between projects\\, and\r\n  front devs will finally get the full ownership of design implementatio\r\n ns.\\n\\nIt will also be the opportunity to clean large parts of the rend\r\n ering pipeline by finalizing the split between UI logic and business lo\r\n gic.\\n\\nWe will explore together how we can use those new UI components\r\n  programmatically in front and back development.  \\n\\nAnd we will disco\r\n ver exciting demos about their use from Admin UI\\, leveraging them as F\r\n ield Widgets to build an Entity Form Display.\\n\\n**Learning Objectives*\r\n *\\n\\nHow to build and share UI components for form inputs  \\n\\nHow to u\r\n se them in projects\\, both programmatically and from Admin UI\\n\\n**Expe\r\n rience level**  \\nIntermediate\\n\\nSpeaker: Pierre Dureau\\n\\nTrack: deve\r\n lopment\\, ai & agentic architecture\\n\\nhttps://events.drupal.org/rotter\r\n -Center--Bringing-AI-Context-Natively-to-Drupal-CMS@events/drupalcon/eu\r\n /2026-rotterdam.json\r\nDTSTAMP:20260830T220900Z\r\nDTSTART:20260929T122500Z\r\nDTEND:20260929T131000Z\r\nSUMMARY:Context Control Center: Bringing AI Context Natively to Drupal C\r\n MS\r\nLOCATION:Van Oldenbarnevelt Room · Postillion Hotel & Convention Centre \r\n WTC Rotterdam\\, Rotterdam\r\nDESCRIPTION:Your AI features are only as good as the knowledge behind th\r\n em. Context Control Center is how Drupal CMS keeps that knowledge struc\r\n tured\\, scoped\\, and ready for every agent and request. Whether you are\r\n  powering help desks\\, personalized experiences\\, automated emails\\, or\r\n  site search\\, the same governed library feeds them all.\\n\\n**Prerequis\r\n ite**\\n\\n- Familiarity with Drupal CMS (or comparable website site buil\r\n ding) at a site builder or digital strategist level: admin UI\\, configu\r\n ration\\, and how content and structure fit together. No PHP or custom m\r\n odule knowledge expected.\\n\\n- A basic sense that Drupal AI can power d\r\n ifferent jobs (for example assistance in the admin UI\\, support-style a\r\n nswers\\, or search help) through agents or similar configuration. You d\r\n o not need to have installed any AI module or recipe beforehand.\\n\\n**T\r\n arget Audience**\\n\\nSite builders\\, CMS administrators\\, digital strate\r\n gists\\, and technical leads who shape AI-enabled experiences on Drupal \r\n CMS. These roles turn organizational knowledge into structured context\\\r\n , decide how it is scoped across agents and site sections\\, and keep AI\r\n  aligned with the organization without custom development.\\n\\n**Outline\r\n **\\n\\nAI in Drupal only looks “smart” when the model knows your organiz\r\n ation’s facts\\, policies\\, and constraints. That knowledge typically li\r\n ves in Slack threads\\, PDFs\\, and ad-hoc prompts\\, so outputs can drift\r\n  and contradict each other. The hard problem is not picking an AI model\r\n \\; it is keeping truth structured\\, current\\, and attached to the right\r\n  workflow.\\n\\nContext Control Center (CCC) is the native context layer \r\n in Drupal CMS: a place to author\\, review\\, translate\\, and reuse conte\r\n xt items for AI features and agents. Instead of everyone pasting their \r\n own detailed prompt\\, Drupal assembles the right context from one gover\r\n ned library per agent and request. That same library can power help des\r\n ks with accurate facts and escalation rules\\, automated emails with req\r\n uired policy text\\, personalized experiences with region-appropriate gu\r\n idance\\, forms where AI follows shared definitions\\, and site search wi\r\n th clear terms and synonyms.\\n\\nWe’ll cover:\\n\\n- Context scopes\\, such\r\n  as language\\, site section\\, and use case\\, that ensure the right cont\r\n ext is applied\\, so support answers never mix with marketing messaging \r\n and personalization doesn’t affect the wrong experience\\n\\n- Remote con\r\n text sources (documentation sites\\, analytics summaries\\, trusted APIs)\r\n  that keep context fresh while flowing through CCC governance\\, scoping\r\n \\, and token limits\\n\\n- Best practices for structuring\\, sizing\\, and \r\n maintaining context so it stays usable and effective alongside Drupal’s\r\n  AI safety and monitoring tools\\n\\n**Learning Objectives**\\n\\nAfter thi\r\n s session\\, participants will be able to:\\n\\n1. Explain why Context Con\r\n trol Center is the native context layer in Drupal CMS and how it replac\r\n es scattered prompts\\, PDFs\\, and wikis with one governed library.\\n\\n2\r\n .
